user_saw: An operator whose config or include file already contained invalid UTF-8 bytes would see openclaw config set succeed while those bytes were silently turned into replacement characters, also in rotated backups; no such report was filed.
summary: Ordinary config writes now strictly decode the original root and include files with decodeUtf8Input before staging backups and refuse with '<path> must be valid UTF-8.' instead of rewriting malformed bytes.
reasoning: The lossy `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` reread in the write guard is long-standing code (blame reaches the shallow graft and 78ca70be only moved it); the fix is one of a series of malformed-UTF-8 hardening sweeps (#167251, #180861, #179022, #186476) that add strict decoding to rewriters, found by audit rather than a user report. It changes policy from lossy success to refusal for already-corrupt input, so I classify it as hardening without a reported failure; if counted as a defect it would be never-worked in pre-graft config I/O whose introducing commit I did not trace.
